ev.mar_betrothal.title: Betrothed
ev.mar_betrothal.text: One evening your parents called you in and told you: you are betrothed. The grown-ups settled everything themselves - the {g:bride|groom}, the wedding gifts, the day of a wedding still years away. Nobody asked what you thought: this is how marriages are made here.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.IND: The priest compared horoscopes, your parents agreed on the dowry - and you were betrothed. Your {g:bride|groom} is of your own caste and a good family; you have never met. The wedding will be soon, but you will live together only once you are older.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.CHN: The matchmaker brought a red card with the eight characters of your birth, the diviner said the signs agree, and the families exchanged betrothal gifts. You are betrothed. You have never laid eyes on your {g:bride|groom} - and will not until the wedding.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.BYZ: The law allows children to be betrothed from the age of seven, and your parents did not wait. A priest blessed the betrothal; the families exchanged gifts and rings. The wedding will be when you turn {g:fourteen|twelve}.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.RUS: The matchmakers came, your parents struck hands and drank to the bargain. You are betrothed. Your elders chose your {g:bride|groom} - by family, by household, by dowry. The wedding will be when you are older.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.ISL: The elders of two families agreed on the marriage and on the mahr, the bridal gift. You are betrothed. Custom says your consent should be asked, but everything is already decided.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.WAF: {g:Your family took|The groom's family brought} the first gifts - kola nuts and cloth - and they were accepted. That means you are betrothed. The wedding will come in a few years, once the whole bridewealth is gathered.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.ETH: Your parents agreed on a marriage, and the elders and a priest witnessed the promise. You are betrothed. Girls are married very young here, so the wedding will not be long in coming.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.ANE: {g:Your family took|The groom's family brought} the terhatum, the bride-price, and a scribe wrote the terms of the marriage on a clay tablet. You are betrothed, though you still play in the yard with the other children.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.JPN: Through a go-between, your parents arranged a marriage with a family of their own standing. You are betrothed. Houses are bound this way from childhood; feelings have nothing to do with it.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.EUR: Your parents signed a marriage contract with another family: land to land, dowry to inheritance. You are betrothed, and you have seen your {g:bride|groom} only once, in church. The wedding will be when you are older.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.rome: By Roman custom a betrothal, the sponsalia, can be made from the age of seven. The families agreed on the dowry and an iron ring was put on your finger. The wedding will be when you turn twelve.
ev.mar_betrothal.text.athens: Your family and your groom made the promise of marriage, the engyē, before witnesses: dowry, date, terms. The groom is much older; you have only glimpsed him. The wedding will be when you turn fourteen.
ev.mar_betrothal.obey.ok: The grown-ups are pleased: you do not argue with your elders, as is proper.
ev.mar_betrothal.hide.ok: They found you in the shed, wiped your tears and spent a long time explaining that this is the way of things. The betrothal stands all the same.
ev.mar_betrothal.ask.ok: They told you a little: what family {g:she|he} comes from, how old {g:she|he} is, what the family is known for. The rest you will learn at the wedding.

ev.mar_wedding_f.title: The wedding
ev.mar_wedding_f.text: The day your family agreed on has come. You have been dressed and braided, and soon you will be led out of your home to songs and weeping. The groom is a grown man and a stranger; today you will see him almost for the first time.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.IND: You are dressed in red and your hands are painted with henna. Today you will walk around the sacred fire with the groom seven times and become his wife. You are seeing him for the first time.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.CHN: A red bridal sedan chair has been sent for you. Your hair is dressed like a woman's and your face hidden under a red veil. In the groom's house you will bow to Heaven and Earth, to his ancestors - and to each other. You have not yet seen his face.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.RUS: Your friends have sung the bride's laments, and your single braid will be undone into two, as married women wear it. Today is the church wedding, and then you will go to the groom's house and his kin. You barely know him.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.BYZ: You have turned twelve, and by law you may marry. In church you and the groom will be crowned, and then a torchlit procession will lead you to his house.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.ISL: The qadi has written the marriage contract and the mahr has been paid. You are dressed in silk, your hands painted with henna, and the women sang at the door all night. In the morning you will be taken to the groom's house.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.JPN: You will be carried to the groom's house in a palanquin, dressed in white - the colour in which one leaves one's own family for good. There you will share three sips from three cups of sake and become part of another house.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.EUR: At the church door the priest will ask whether you consent. Your elders gave the answer long ago: the dowry is counted, the contract signed. The groom is many years older; you have seen him twice.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.ETH: You were led out to the groom in white. The priest will bless you and the guests will feast for three days. You are still a girl, and by custom you will spend the first years mostly with your own family.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.WAF: The bridewealth is gathered and accepted, and the griots sing of the two families. The women braided your hair all night, and in the morning you will go to the groom's house and his large family.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.ANE: The bride-price is paid and the tablet with the marriage terms is sealed. Today in the groom's house you will be veiled - a sign that you are no longer a girl but a married woman.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.rome: You are twelve - by Roman law old enough to marry. Your hair has been parted into six locks, you wear the flame-orange veil, and in the evening a torchlit procession will lead you to the groom's house.
ev.mar_wedding_f.text.athens: You are fourteen. You have given your toys to Artemis - childhood is over. In the evening a cart will take you to the groom's house, with torches carried behind it.
ev.mar_wedding_f.obey.ok: You are married. A new family, a new house, new duties - and not one familiar face.
ev.mar_wedding_f.plead: Beg your family to wait a year or two
ev.mar_wedding_f.plead.success: Your family is angry but agrees to put off the wedding. Not for long.
ev.mar_wedding_f.plead.failure: No one listens. The wedding took place on the appointed day.
ev.mar_wedding_m.title: You are to be married
ev.mar_wedding_m.text: The match was made long ago and the gifts are gathered - your elders have decided it is time for the wedding. You are too young to think of a household of your own, but nobody asked you. You hardly know the bride.
ev.mar_wedding_m.text.IND: They set you on a horse in a wedding turban, and a procession with drums carried you to the bride's house. You will walk around the sacred fire, but you will live together only when the families judge you old enough.
ev.mar_wedding_m.text.RUS: The matchmakers have done their work: today is the church wedding. You have no moustache yet, but at home they already call you the young master. You saw the bride once, at the viewing, and only for a moment.
ev.mar_wedding_m.text.CHN: Today a red sedan chair will be sent for the bride. Together you will bow to Heaven, Earth and the ancestors of your family - and you will count as a grown man, though your beard has not yet started to grow.
ev.mar_wedding_m.text.BYZ: You are fourteen - by law old enough to marry. The bride was chosen from a family of your own standing. In church you will both be crowned, and afterwards the whole quarter will feast.
ev.mar_wedding_m.text.JPN: Your elders and the go-between have arranged everything: today the bride will be brought to your house. You will share three sips from three cups of sake, and the alliance of two houses will be sealed.
ev.mar_wedding_m.obey.ok: The wedding was loud and merry. Now you have a wife - as young as you are, and just as lost.
ev.mar_wedding_m.plead: Ask for more time: you are not ready
ev.mar_wedding_m.plead.success: Your elders grumble but agree to wait a year or two.
ev.mar_wedding_m.plead.failure: "Ready or not, this is the custom," your elders said. The wedding took place.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.title: A bride chosen for you
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text: Your parents have announced that a bride has been found. A suitable family, a good dowry, and the diviners have no objection. You have never seen her - and by custom you should not until the wedding.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.IND: Your parents found a bride of your own caste, and the priest compared horoscopes. The dowry has been discussed and an auspicious day chosen. Your consent is a formality.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.CHN: The matchmaker went round half the city and found a bride "of matching gates" - from a family of the same standing. Your parents are pleased. You were asked - out of politeness.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.RUS: Your parents sent the matchmakers, and they came back with good news: you are to have a girl from the neighbouring farm, hard-working and with a dowry. The viewing is set, and the wedding will be after the autumn feast of the Intercession.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.ISL: The women of your family chose a bride for you: they visited her home, saw her at the bathhouse and were satisfied. The elders have already agreed on the mahr.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.JPN: Through a go-between your parents found a bride from a house of your standing. Today is the miai, the formal meeting: you sit facing each other without raising your eyes, and only the grown-ups speak.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.AMR: Your parents called in the old matchmaker women; they carried gifts to the girl's house and came back with the answer: yes. The bride was chosen for you - that is the custom.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.cusco: Each year the Inca's governor gathers the young men and women and pairs them off himself. Your turn has come: a bride has been assigned to you, and her family has already agreed.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.quito: Each year the Inca's governor gathers the young men and women and pairs them off himself. Your turn has come: a bride has been assigned to you, and her family has already agreed.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.MAY: Through a matchmaker your parents came to terms with the bride's family. For several years you will work for her kin - that is how a wife is paid for here.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.EUR: Your elders struck a bargain with the neighbours: the bride brings a riverside meadow and a cow as her dowry. Whether you love her is beside the point.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.text.WAF: The elders of your lineage chose a bride for you and have already taken kola nuts to her family. Now you will spend years helping her kin and saving for the bridewealth.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.obey.ok: The wedding was held a few months later. You only got a proper look at your bride at the feast.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.see: Ask to see her at least once
ev.mar_bride_chosen.see.success: A meeting was arranged in front of the families. She smiled at you secretly, and suddenly you felt at ease. The wedding was held in autumn.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.see.failure: "Whatever next!" your elders cried. The wedding went ahead as proper, and at home they looked at you askance for a long time.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.refuse: Refuse: you will marry whom you choose
ev.mar_bride_chosen.refuse.success: Your family is furious, but the match fell through. You are your own master - for now.
ev.mar_bride_chosen.refuse.failure: Nobody listened. The wedding took place, and the resentment remained.
ev.mar_m_matchmakers.text: Matchmakers came to see your parents. You were sent out into the yard, but through the wall you heard the grown-ups slowly bargaining over someone's wedding - perhaps your own.
ev.mar_m_matchmakers.text.CHN: A matchmaker came with red cards and drank tea with your parents for a long time. You listened behind the screen: they were talking about someone's eight characters of fate - maybe yours.
ev.mar_m_matchmakers.text.IND: Guests came with horoscopes and sweets. The grown-ups spent a long time reckoning by the stars and arguing about a dowry. You were sent off to play, but you understood: somewhere a match is already being sought for you.
ev.mar_m_matchmakers.text.AMR: The old matchmaker women came with gifts, and your parents received them with honour. They talked of someone's wedding - you listened behind the door, holding your breath.
ev.mar_m_new_home.text: You live in your husband's house now, among his kin. You get up before everyone, carry water, grind grain and wait to hear what your mother-in-law will say. In the evenings you long to go home to your own people.
ev.mar_m_new_home.text.IND: In your husband's house you rise in the dark, first of all, and go to bed last. Your mother-in-law checks every flatbread. You are allowed to visit your own family only at festivals.
ev.mar_m_new_home.text.CHN: In your husband's house you wait on your mother-in-law: in the morning you bring her water to wash, in the evening her tea. Your old family is now "outer kin", and you may see them only rarely.
ev.mar_m_new_home.text.RUS: In your husband's house the mother-in-law, the bolshukha, runs everything. You are the youngest daughter-in-law: yours to stoke the stove, carry water and keep quiet when scolded. You are not let home even for a day.
ev.mar_m_new_home.text.JPN: In your husband's house you rank last of all. Your mother-in-law teaches you the ways of the house: how to bow, how to serve, how to stay silent.
ev.mar_m_child_bride.text: You are a married woman now, yet a rag doll still hides in your chest. Your sisters-in-law snigger; your mother-in-law pretends not to notice.
ev.mar_m_boy_husband.text: You were married off as a mere boy. You and your young wife are more like two children than husband and wife: by day you squabble over trifles, and in the evening you listen together to the old folks' tales.
